gladiator_mk1_belgium: Belgium bought 22 Gladiators in the late 1930s, 15 from Gloster and seven put together locally by SABCA, and flew them with its 'Comet' squadron mainly as trainers; nearly all of those still airworthy were wiped out within the first two days of the German invasion in May 1940. In the game it handles just like the British, Chinese and Swedish Gladiators, so anyone who has flown those will feel at home, and newcomers get a dependable, forgiving turn-fighter. Added in the "Seek & Destroy" update, it opens the BeNeLux subtree of the French tree.
gladiator_mk1_china: China ordered 36 Gloster Gladiators in late 1937, and on their combat debut over Nanjing in February 1938 Chinese pilots downed two Japanese A5Ms; the arrival of the A6M and a lack of spares later pushed the survivors into training units. In the game it turns very well and hits hard for a biplane, but it climbs only modestly and sheds speed quickly when pulled hard, so close-in dogfights suit it best. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision" and wears the colours of Chinese ace Arthur Chin by default.
gladiator_mk2: Gloster's interwar biplane fighter began as a company venture to replace the Gauntlet and was already outdated by the time it reached RAF squadrons in 1937, yet it served widely at home and abroad and produced several aces; the Mk II, with a slightly uprated Mercury VIIIA engine, was built 270 times. Its four 7.7 mm guns with incendiary belts are its best asset, readily setting fire to the wood-and-fabric opponents it usually meets. Speed, handling and toughness are only middling for a biplane, though, so both nimbler biplanes and faster monoplanes can get the better of it. It has been in the game since the open beta.
gladiator_mk2_france: A gift variant of the Gladiator Mk II that has existed since the open beta, the Mk IIF once sat among Britain's reserve aircraft until it and the Mk IIS were swapped out for the Fury and Nimrod. Doing well in it takes effort, particularly in Realistic Battles: agile biplanes such as the CR.42, F3F-2 and Ki-10 are already a handful, and uptiers add monoplanes like the P-40E, I-16, Ki-43 and Bf 109, each holding some edge over it. That can make the early grind feel slow.
gladiator_mk2_navy: The Fleet Air Arm's carrier version of the Gladiator added a tail hook, catapult fittings, a strengthened airframe and a belly-mounted dinghy while keeping the Mk II's guns; 98 were completed, 38 of them converted from existing Mk IIs. It flies much like its RAF counterpart: quick for a biplane and far more agile than the monoplanes it meets, yet neither as nimble as the lighter biplanes nor as fast as the monoplanes, which makes it a balanced all-rounder rather than a specialist. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
gladiator_mk2_silver: The Mk IIS was given away just once, at the February 2015 "Gladiator Glory!" event, and has been unobtainable since; like the Mk IIF it used to be one of Britain's reserve fighters before the Fury and Nimrod replaced them. It is not an easy aircraft to succeed in, above all in Realistic Battles, where it meets nimble biplanes such as the CR.42, F3F and Ki-10 and, when uptiered, faster types like the P-40E, I-16, Ki-43 and Bf 109, all of which have advantages of their own.
gladiator_mk2_tuck: This Gladiator Mk II carries the markings of Robert Stanford Tuck, who flew the type with No. 65 Squadron and destroyed 29 enemy aircraft between 1939 and 1942 before being taken prisoner. The Mk II, the RAF's last biplane fighter, differed from the Mk I mainly in its more powerful Mercury VIIIA/AS engine, and 270 were built. In combat it is well armed and very manoeuvrable, ranking among the stronger biplanes for dogfighting, though it climbs poorly and bleeds its limited speed in hard turns. It arrived in Update 1.31.
go229_v3: The Horten brothers' jet flying wing began in 1943 as a fast-bomber project and was later reworked as a cheap fighter, with Gotha using plywood wings to cut costs; the unfinished V3 prototype was captured by US troops in April 1945 and survives at the Smithsonian. It is startlingly agile for a jet, at times able to out-turn even the P-51H, but hard manoeuvres drain its energy fast, so diving and climbing attacks suit it better than turning fights. It accelerates sluggishly below about 500 km/h yet leaves piston fighters behind above that. Added in Update 1.43, it was the first jet of the German Zerstörer line.
h-75a-1_france: The first Curtiss Hawks bought by France, the H-75A-1 was an export model of the American P-36, ordered as a batch of 100 when French industry could not supply enough modern fighters on its own. The aircraft arrived in December 1938 and were assembled in France, with French modifications to the weapons, controls and instrument panel. Orders for the A-2, A-3 and A-4 followed, and French Hawks went on to fight for the Free French and the British and, through captured airframes, for Finland. It joined the game in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
h-75a-2_finland: An American-built Hawk sold to France, seized by Germany at the armistice and passed on to Finland for use against the Soviet Union, this H-75A-2 sits in the German tree as a premium. The A-2 was France's rush order of 100 aircraft, improving on the A-1 with extra guns and a better engine. It was first handed out in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy" to players of the opening public World War mode season and is now a rare item on the War Thunder Market.
h-75a-4_france: The H-75A-4 was one of several Curtiss Hawk batches, export relatives of the US P-36, that France bought because its own factories could not build modern fighters fast enough. Only a few of the A-4s ever reached France; most were redirected to Britain, which flew them as the Mohawk. French Hawks kept fighting throughout the war under Free French and British control, and captured examples were also flown by Finland against the Soviets. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
h-75m_china: The H-75M was the most numerous Curtiss Hawk in Chinese service, a simplified export model with fixed landing gear and a less powerful Wright Cyclone engine; 112 were ordered, and the first 30 went straight into combat in mid-1938. Short of trained pilots, spare parts and ground crew, China soon lost every one of them, and they achieved little. In the game it weighs less than the American P-36 and turns slightly better, but the weaker engine and draggier airframe leave it noticeably slower. It was the reward for the 2025 Winter Concert event.
h145m: Airbus Helicopters' H145M is the military development of the EC645 T2, certified in 2015; Germany was the launch customer, taking 15 for special-operations support with the 64th Helicopter Squadron at Laupheim, and Thailand, Serbia, Hungary and Luxembourg followed. In the game its twin engines give brisk acceleration and forgiving handling, backed by thermal sights, countermeasures, Spike ER missiles for heavy armour and laser-guided FZ275 rockets for light vehicles and helicopters. Its weak point is air-to-air firepower, limited to either twin 12.7 mm machine guns or two 20 mm M.621 cannons. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
h6k4: Kawanishi's four-engined Type 97 flying boat, shaped by the company's experience with Short Brothers designs, entered navy service in 1938 and could stay on patrol for a full day; 215 were built before the H8K took over. In the game it can strike bases and ships with a pair of 800 kg bombs or torpedoes, which may fall short of destroying a base, and it can capture zones in naval battles. Its size and low speed make it an easy target, and most of its defensive guns are feeble 7.7 mm weapons, so the lone 20 mm tail cannon does most of the defending. It has been in the game since the open beta.
h8k2: Successor to the H6K, the Type 2 flying boat stretched range to around 7,400 km, well beyond the B-17 or even the B-29, and its heavy defensive firepower earned it a fearsome reputation among Allied pilots. For all its bulk it is one of the toughest bombers at its rank: strong engines, plenty of fuel, a sturdy airframe and a battery of 20 mm cannons that can knock down a pursuer with one good burst, plus more agility than its size suggests. The catch is a modest 1.6-tonne bomb load. It came with Update 1.57 "Battle March".
h8k3: The Model 22 was an attempt to clean up the H8K2's aerodynamics with retractable wing floats, also adding a dorsal gun position and extra armour around the fuselage fuel tanks, but two tonnes of added weight cancelled out the gains, so only two prototypes were built, later re-engined as H8K4s. With the floats tucked away they were often mistaken for B-24 Liberators. In the game the reduced drag gives it better acceleration than the H8K2 and the added armour makes it even harder to bring down, while bombs, guns and general handling stay the same. It was added in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
h_34_france: Sikorsky's piston-engined H-34, with its radial engine in the nose driving the rotor through a shaft that runs past the cockpit, was assembled or licence-built in France by Sud-Aviation in about 300 examples, and logged more than 190,000 flying hours in Algeria, much of it evacuating troops. In the game it is a large, unwieldy and unarmoured target, but it is quick, holding around 300 km/h in level flight, and carries bombs, rockets and ATGMs for dealing with armour, so enemy anti-aircraft vehicles are best avoided rather than challenged. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
halifax_mk3: Handley Page's Halifax started as a backup to the Vulture-engined Avro Manchester and was reworked with four engines; when Merlins were reserved for fighters and the Lancaster, the Mk III switched to Bristol Hercules radials and became the main production model, with 2,091 built out of 6,178 Halifaxes in total. In the game it handles with surprising agility for a heavy bomber, which helps with bomb runs and escapes, and its payload of almost six tonnes can flatten bases and ground targets. Both the airframe and the defensive guns are fragile, though, so avoiding fighters matters more than fighting them. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
harrier_frs1: The Royal Navy's Sea Harrier made its name in the 1982 Falklands War, where the type shot down 21 Argentine aircraft without losing any of its own in the air; this version reflects a later upgrade allowing four AIM-9L Sidewinders on twin rails. In the game it builds on the Harrier GR.3 with a radar, which few Harriers in the game have, and the far more lethal AIM-9L, making it a much stronger air-to-air fighter. The price is extra weight and slightly duller handling than its contemporaries. It is a squadron vehicle, introduced in the "Apex Predators" update, and a good stepping stone towards the Harrier GR.7.
harrier_frs1_early: The early-service Sea Harrier FRS.1 joined the Royal Navy in 1980, combining the Harrier GR.3 design with a Blue Fox radar, a bubble canopy and a single pair of AIM-9L Sidewinders; more missile pylons and Sea Eagle capability came only after the Falklands. It flies like the game's other Harriers, with quick acceleration that gets it into the fight early and full VTOL ability. Its radar and two AIM-9Ls cover air combat, but it has no guided air-to-ground weapons, only five 1,000 lb bombs: enough to destroy a base, though dedicated strikers such as the Jaguar are better at hunting tanks. It was added in the "Sons of Attila" update.
harrier_gr1: Growing out of the P.1127 and Kestrel vectored-thrust prototypes, the Harrier GR.1 entered RAF service in 1969 as a ground-attack and reconnaissance jet able to operate from almost anywhere, and it was used to trial the British SRAAM short-range missile. In the game it takes off and lands vertically and carries SRAAMs, bombs and rockets, doing its best work low down where VTOL tricks can catch opponents off guard. It is slow and not especially agile, and with no chaff or flares it is exposed to missiles, although its SRAAMs can be used to shoot down incoming missiles head-on. It arrived in the "New Power" update.
harrier_gr3: An upgraded Harrier that entered RAF service in 1976, the GR.3 gained a stronger Pegasus Mk 103 engine, a nose laser rangefinder and target seeker, a radar warning receiver, chaff and flare dispensers and the ability to carry Sidewinders; 102 were built or converted, and in the Falklands they flew 126 sorties for four losses to enemy fire. In the game it keeps the family's vertical take-off and landing, but AIM-9G missiles and countermeasures make it far more capable against aircraft than the GR.1. That frees it from hugging the ground: it can work from higher altitude and use its Sidewinders on targets below. It came in the "New Power" update.
harrier_gr7: Britain's version of the McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II, the GR.7 developed the GR.5 with night and all-weather equipment: FLIR, digital terrain mapping, night-vision goggle compatibility and Paveway guided bombs. It flew in the Balkans, Iraq and Afghanistan before retirement in late 2010. In the game its newer Pegasus engine makes it faster than the earlier Harriers, and it brings a strong strike kit of Paveway II and III bombs and AGM-65 Mavericks, plus AIM-9M missiles for self-defence. Manoeuvrability is lacking, though, and it carries only a few air-to-air missiles. It arrived in Update 2.19 "Drone Age".
harrier_t10: After older two-seat Harriers proved inadequate trainers for the GR.7, the RAF ordered 13 T.10s in 1990, built with GR.7 avionics and kept fully combat-capable; the first flew in April 1994, and despite the trainer label they served in front-line units until the Harrier left RAF service around 2011. In the game it is close to the GR.7, with plenty of countermeasures and a broad choice of bombs and other air-to-ground stores, but it lacks AIM-9M missiles and flies less well. Its low top speed makes both air combat and escaping missiles difficult. It was added in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
hawk_200: The Hawk 200 was British Aerospace's dedicated light combat version of the Hawk, a jet trainer family of which over 1,000 were built; it first flew in 1986, and 62 went to Oman, Malaysia and Indonesia. In the game it is fairly slow and only middling in a turn, but it makes up for that with solid weaponry: 30 mm cannons, AIM-9L missiles and a range of air-to-ground stores. Its small airframe is hard to hit, which helps it survive. It came with Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
hawk_200_rda: BAE Systems built the Hawk 200 RDA, airframe ZJ201, in the early 1990s to show export customers that the Hawk 200 could carry Skyflash missiles; it led to the Hawk 205 produced for Saudi Arabia, before the demonstrator itself crashed in Bratislava in June 1999. Compared with the standard Hawk 200 in the game it adds a radar and two Skyflash missiles alongside two AIM-9L slots, but gives up its cannons. Speed and agility remain weak, which makes it hard to get the Skyflashes into a good firing position. It was added in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
hawk_209_indonesia: Indonesia's Hawk 209, bought in 1993, was the most capable member of the Hawk 200 family, with upgraded avionics and radar, and it served as a front-line light attack jet beside the A-4E Skyhawk, including intercept missions against Australian aircraft during the 1999 East Timor withdrawal. It flies exactly like the British Hawk 200 but is armed differently: a single 30 mm ADEN Mk.4 cannon, AIM-9P-4s rather than AIM-9Ls, AGM-65G instead of AGM-65B, only FFAR Mighty Mouse rockets and no retarded bombs. Both share the Sea Eagle, one of the strongest anti-ship missiles in the game. It joined the Japanese tree in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
hawk_iii: Curtiss built the Hawk III as an export derivative of the BF2C Goshawk, with an improved Cyclone engine and room for more bombs, and China became its biggest user, fighting with it over Shanghai and Nanjing where several pilots became aces despite facing better Japanese monoplanes. Next to the American BF2C-1 it is faster than most biplanes it meets and carries a sizeable load for its size, a 500 lb bomb plus four 100 lb bombs. Its two machine guns are a weak point, but it can still hold its own as a fighter and is at its best supporting ground forces. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
hawk_t1a: As the airframes of its Hawk T Mk 1 and 1A trainers neared the end of their lives, the RAF rebuilt them in the 1990s and 2000s under a Fuselage Replacement Programme that swapped the centre and rear fuselage, changing the look slightly but not the performance; they flew on until the early 2010s. In the game it is a small, light jet aimed at ground attack with a modest choice of underwing stores. It handles much like the Hawk 200 apart from differences in weight and thrust, and because its opponents are less dangerous it can hold its own in a dogfight. It came in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
hawk_t1a_early: The Hawk began as a Hawker Siddeley private venture to replace the RAF's Folland Gnat trainer, first flying in 1974 and selling more than 1,000 examples worldwide, including to the United States as the T-45. The T Mk 1A could carry external weapons such as a 30 mm ADEN gun pod, and 89 were built to take over the short-range interceptor role from the Hawker Hunter. In the game it is a light, compact ground-attack jet with limited stores, handling close to the Hawk 200 bar its weight and engine power, and it is a capable dogfighter against the weaker aircraft it meets. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
he-111h-16_winter: A late He 111 H, the H-16 combined Jumo 211 F-2 engines, roughly a third more powerful than the original H's Jumo 211 A-1s, with heavier defensive guns that included a 20 mm cannon in the nose and a 13 mm MG 131. It is arguably the strongest He 111 in the game: it misses out on the H-6's Fritz X guided bomb but can lift the huge SC2500, a bomb of about 2.4 tonnes, and the nose cannon gives head-on attackers something to think about. The uprated engines overheat quickly on WEP, so emergency power needs careful rationing. It has been in the game since the open beta.
he-111h-2: Built from late 1939 into early 1940, the H-3 differed only slightly from the H-2, mainly in its Jumo 211 D-1 engines, while over the H-1 it gained cockpit armour, external racks for bombs and three more MG 15s; 504 were produced. In the game its jobs are hitting bases in Air Battles and helping friendly tanks in mixed battles, and it brings a fair bomb load, a well-glazed nose with a good view, capable defensive gunners and decent speed. On the other hand it cannot absorb much damage and handles only moderately for a bomber. It has been in the game since the open beta.
he-111h-6: A veteran of the open beta, the He 111 H-6 is a medium bomber with more flexibility than it first appears: loadouts range from more than 30 light bombs to two 1,000 kg bombs plus a 250 kg one, enough to destroy a base, or a single Fritz X guided bomb. The airframe tears apart easily, so steep dive-bombing in the style of earlier German bombers is a bad idea. Its defensive guns fire quickly but are weak and inaccurate, so staying away from enemy fighters is the safest plan.
he-162a-1: Heinkel's answer to the Volksjäger call for a cheap, simple jet fighter flew just 74 days after the design was chosen; the A-1 carried two MK 108 cannons, but rushed development brought reliability problems, and only a few of the roughly 120 built saw combat before the war ended. In the game its weak, overheat-prone engine limits climb, yet top speed is enough to outrun piston fighters, so hit-and-run passes suit it, and its light airframe turns respectably when needed. One cannon hit can wreck even a bomber, but with 50 rounds per gun and slow shells, landing hits is hard. It first appeared as a 5th-anniversary event reward.
he-162a-2: The He 162's distinctive back-mounted jet engine was easy to service and stayed clear of runway debris; on the A-2, the A-1's vibration-prone MK 108s gave way to the 20 mm MG 151, and pilots rated it stable to fly. Among the earliest jets in the game, it mostly meets piston aircraft, which it can outrun and chase down with a top speed of about 840 km/h, but just 910 kgf of thrust makes acceleration painfully slow. Repeated slashing passes on slower targets work better than turning fights, though it is nimble enough to cope with propeller fighters if cornered. It has been in the game since the open beta.
he-177a-3: Heinkel's Greif came from the 1936 Bomber A requirement but only reached mass production in 1942; the A-3 had a longer fuselage, relocated oil tanks and engines less prone to fires, and 148 of the 612 built could carry guided bombs. In the game it pairs good speed with a heavy payload, strong defensive guns and both Fritz X and Hs 293 guided bombs, the Hs 293 being the main difference from the A-5. Its flaws are the same as that model's: a big silhouette, engines that heat up fast and little range on one engine. It was the Battle Pass Season 17 "Guided Fury" reward.
he-177a-5: Built to a demanding pre-war specification for a fast long-range heavy bomber, the Greif reached service too late to matter, with around 1,000 built, and became infamous for engine fires caused by poor cooling. What looks like a twin-engined aircraft actually has four engines, paired to drive two propellers, and in the game they still overheat if run hard for long. An airframe rated to 683 km/h lets it dive onto bases quickly, and six turrets give it excellent defensive coverage, making it a capable, self-reliant bomber despite its troubled history. It arrived in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm" as a Revenue Share model by Daniil "Joy_Division__" Zaytsev.
he51a1: Designed by the Günter brothers and passed off as a trainer while the Luftwaffe was still secret, the He 51 entered production in 1933 but was soon outdated; it beat older biplanes in Spain until modern Soviet aircraft arrived, and von Richthofen later shaped his close-support tactics while flying one. In the game it is slow and lightly armed with two machine guns, but a turn time of about 15 seconds makes it very hard to out-turn. Picking off single targets works better than diving into a furball, tracer belts suit fabric-covered aircraft, and a few hits can slow a faster monoplane enough to finish it.
he51b1: Germany's He 51 B-1 biplane has been in the game since the open beta. It is neither fast nor heavily armed, its two light machine guns falling short of some early Soviet fighters, but it holds its own among other reserve aircraft. Singling out one target beats diving into a crowded dogfight, and its low-speed agility can get it out of trouble when cornered. Tracer belts work best against fabric-covered aircraft with unprotected fuel tanks, and even faster monoplanes can be turned on and crippled with a few hits.
he51b_2w: A float-equipped He 51 given away as a gift, the B-2/H has been around since the open beta and has returned several times: as a reward for War Thunder's 2014 birthday and the 2015 Day of German Unity, in Warbond shop trophies from April 2019, and in the "10 rare vehicles" event for the game's 10th anniversary in 2022. It is slow and its pair of machine guns hits lightly, yet its agility lets it cope with other reserve fighters and slip away when cornered. It is most effective picking off single targets rather than joining large furballs, with tracer belts doing the most damage to fabric-covered aircraft.
he51c1: The C was the ground-attack member of the He 51 family, with 100 built as light attack aircraft; as a fighter the Günter brothers' biplane had been outclassed once modern Soviet types reached Spain. In the game it is slow and lightly armed, but agile enough to hold its own among reserve fighters and escape tight spots. It does best taking on one target at a time, with tracers working well against fabric-covered aircraft, and a few hits can slow even a faster monoplane enough to catch it. It has been in the game since the open beta.
he51c1_late: This gift version of the He 51 C-1 has existed since the open beta but is now hidden and cannot be obtained. In the game it behaves like the other He 51s: slow and armed with just two machine guns, yet manoeuvrable enough to compete among reserve fighters and wriggle out of trouble. It works best singling out one opponent at a time, tracer belts suit fabric-covered targets with unprotected tanks, and a few well-placed hits can slow a faster monoplane enough to finish it off.
he_100d_1: Heinkel's He 100 D-1 is the fastest aircraft at its rank and climbs very well, making it a natural boom-and-zoom fighter that attacks, extends or zooms away, and comes back; flown with discipline it can dominate a match. Its weak spot is a cooling system spread through the nose and wings, where around seven in ten hits start a water leak that soon forces a return to base, so even a stray round can end a sortie. Firepower is also thin, with three 7.92 mm MG 17s that struggle against bombers and armoured targets, and ammunition is limited. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
he_112a_0: Heinkel's He 112 lost the Luftwaffe fighter contest to the cheaper, simpler Bf 109, and this A-0 (V6) was a one-off from 1936 with a 20 mm cannon firing through the propeller shaft; sent to Spain, it flew ground-attack sorties for around six months, destroying an armoured train among other targets, before a landing accident wrecked it. In the game the "Kanonenflieger" is tough, dives safely at high speed and turns well, and its single cannon has flat, accurate ballistics for long-range shots at aircraft or vehicles depending on the belt. That makes it especially useful for ground attack in combined battles. It has been in the game since the open beta.
he_112b_0: The B-0 is the most developed He 112 in the game and works best as an all-rounder: it can outpace agile biplanes, out-turn heavier monoplanes, and its firepower, the same as the Bf 109 E-3's, quickly finishes off bombers. Speed is decent for its rank yet still behind the LaGG-3, Yaks, F2A Buffalo and P-36 it often meets, and biplanes, as well as nimble Japanese types like the Ki-27 and A5M4, will always win a turning fight against it. Climb is unremarkable, but a 690 km/h limit lets it survive fast dives. It leads on to the Bf 109 B-1/L in the research tree and has been in the game since the open beta.
he_112b_1: This premium He 112 B-1/U2 wears the markings of the Hungarian Air Force. It has been in the game since the open beta but left the store in the "Danger Zone" update, when an equivalent aircraft joined the Italian tree. Nimble and easy to fly, it pairs strong armament with gentle matchmaking, which made it a good way for newer players to speed up progress through the German aviation tree.
he_112b_1_italy: For the B series Heinkel reworked the He 112's airframe and gave it much heavier armament, with 20 mm wing cannons alongside its machine guns; the B-1/U2 export model used the Jumo 210E engine, and Romania's 30 fought on the Eastern Front and later served as trainers until 1947. In the game it is close to the German B-0 apart from its engine and light Romanian camouflage. Its guns are dangerous even to multi-engined bombers, it turns well and is better still when attacking from above, and while its level speed is modest, its high dive limit gives it a reliable escape. It joined the Italian tree in Update 2.17 "Danger Zone".
he_112b_2: Available since the open beta, this gift He 112 B-2/U2 was first handed out in the 2014 Thanksgiving sale to players who bought three discounted packs, and later turned up in Warbond shop trophy chests between September 2018 and March 2019 and again from March to November 2020.
he_112v_5: Beaten by the Bf 109 for Luftwaffe orders largely on cost and ease of production, the He 112 was offered abroad, and the V-5 was the export demonstrator shown to six countries, from Austria to Japan, in 1937–38; it was the most refined of the prototypes before the heavily redesigned B series. In the game it is a nimble low-altitude fighter that holds energy well and can be dived hard without flutter, letting it use speed against the many biplanes it meets and tight turning against monoplanes. It is easily damaged, though, and its armament is modest. It has been in the game since the open beta.
he_115a_2_sweden: Sweden's T 2 was the German He 115 A-2 floatplane: twelve arrived before the war and six more were bought when it broke out, and the type served as a torpedo bomber, conventional bomber and long-range reconnaissance aircraft until 1952, popular with crews throughout. In the game it is slow and unremarkable and stands little chance in Air RB, where its size and weak defensive guns make it easy prey for fighters. Ground and naval battles suit it better: well-placed 450 kg or 250 kg bombs can knock out tanks, its torpedo is effective against destroyers, and its floats let it land on water. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
he_115c_1: Heinkel's He 115 floatplane replaced the He 59 in German coastal units from 1939, and kept patrolling against Arctic convoys from Norway after its low speed ended production in 1940. The C-1, from the final production series, had better defensive turrets and a forward-firing 15 mm MG 151 in the nose. In the game it is slow and clumsy even for a bomber and carries only a modest load, but the nose cannon can deal with lightly armoured vehicles or catch careless aircraft. Wide turret arcs do not make up for its fragility, so long fights are best avoided and friendly fighters kept close. It arrived in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila".
he_219a_7: Heinkel built the first He 219 night fighter with its own money, and although the air ministry turned it down, night-fighter chief Josef Kammhuber was so impressed by its first flight in November 1942 that he pushed it into production; the A-7 brought stronger DB 603E engines and more weapon choices. In the game it is a heavy fighter with formidable firepower, a good climb rate, strong survivability and a radar, but no defensive guns, middling speed and agility, and awkward ballistics to master. It came in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows" via the Revenue Share programme, modelled by Daniil "Joy_Division__" Zaitsev.
hellcat_fmk1: Britain's premium Hellcat is practically the same aircraft as the American F6F-5, but its premium bonus to rewards makes it a useful tool for researching British rank IV aircraft. Six 12.7 mm machine guns give it solid firepower, and for ground attack it can add six 127 mm rockets, two 298 mm rockets, two 1,000 lb bombs, or rockets and bombs together. Like its American twin, it is approachable and fun to fly. It has been in the game since the open beta, originally as the Hellcat Mk I, and took its current name in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
hkp2: Sweden's HKP2 was the French Alouette II, first imported in 1957 as a civilian crop-sprayer before being taken up by all three armed services; 29 were operated, ten of them licence-built by SAAB, and the army flew them until the HKP9 replaced them in 1988. In the game it is light and nimble but completely unarmoured. Unlike the French Alouettes it sits on floats rather than skids, but it carries the same RB 52A missiles, a Swedish SS.11, whose 3.5 km reach forces it close to the fighting and into range of anti-aircraft fire. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
hkp3c: The HKP3C traces back to an Italian licence-built Bell 204B bought by Sweden in 1962 for rescue work; after the original HKP3A proved underpowered it gained a stronger engine as the HKP3B, and the army then lengthened the tail and rotor to create the C. Sweden trialled BANTAM anti-tank missiles on it successfully but never bought them for service. In the game it is Sweden's first helicopter and one of the earliest missile-armed ones, meeting relatively primitive opposition while still able to strike from a safe range. Its missiles hit far harder than unguided rockets but fly very slowly, so they reward patience. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
hkp9a_cb2: The HKP9A was Sweden's anti-tank Bo 105, ordered by the FMV procurement agency in the mid-1980s with TOW missiles and the Saab HeliTOW sighting system developed with Emerson Electronics; 21 were delivered and served the army until 2009. Like every Bo 105 in the game it is extremely agile, able to pop up from behind terrain, fire and duck back out of sight before the enemy reacts. Up to eight capable missiles with useful range give it real punch, but with no armour it is very easy prey for aircraft and anti-aircraft guns. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
hkp9a_cb3_fc: While Sweden waited for its 20 HKP9As, the Försökscentralen test centre leased four Bo 105 CB-3s from MBB in 1985; one, used for weapons trials, was later bought outright and became the 21st HKP9A, fitted with an upgraded HeliTOW sight that added a FLIR thermal channel. In the game that translates to BGM-71D TOW-2 missiles able to defeat almost any tank it meets from the front, and a thermal sight that makes spotting targets much easier by day or night. Otherwise it is the same small, agile and unarmoured helicopter as the standard HKP9A. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
hornet_mk1: De Havilland's twin-engined Hornet was conceived at the end of the Second World War as a long-range, high-altitude interceptor, and its endurance suited the Pacific colonies, where bases were few; the Mk.I was the first version, with 60 built out of 383 Hornets in all. Compared with the tech tree Mk.III it is lighter and slightly more agile, though without the Mk.III's 150-octane fuel it has a little less power. Four 20 mm Hispano Mk.V cannons under the nose shred most targets, it climbs and fights well at altitude as an energy fighter, and underwing stores and armour-piercing belts let it contribute in ground battles too. It arrived in the "Hot Tracks" update.
hornet_mk3: De Havilland's Hornet followed the Mosquito and was meant for the Pacific war, entering RAF service as it ended and later flying strikes in Malaya; the Mk.III was the most numerous version, with 132 built. It faces top piston fighters such as the P-51H and Bf 109 K as well as early jets like the F-80C, but an air-spawn start lets it climb high and choose when to dive. It lacks an airbrake, yet it gains speed so reluctantly past about 750 km/h that it can outlast pursuing piston fighters in a dive, and it pulls hard at speed. Big and less nimble than single-engined fighters, it is best kept fast and high.
hp52_hampden_mk1_late: One of the first bombers in the British tree, the Hampden Mk I sets the pattern for the aircraft that follow it: reasonable performance paired with a bomb load heavy for its rank, which can rack up a big score quickly. Its speed lets it reach ground targets ahead of other bombers on maps such as Essen, drop low to rearm at the airfield, and then return at low level with delayed fuses to clear what remains, including bases. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
hp52_hampden_tbmk1: The torpedo-carrying Hampden TB Mk I comes early in the British bomber line and sets the tone for what follows: respectable flight performance married to a payload that can push a player's score into four figures in short order. On maps such as Essen its speed gets it to ground targets ahead of other bombers, after which it can descend to rearm at the airfield and return at low level with delayed fuses to finish the remaining targets or bases. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
hp52_hampden_tbmk1_ussr_utk1: In September 1942, 32 RAF and RAAF Hampden torpedo bombers flew from Shetland to northern Russia to help guard convoy PQ 18; headwinds ruled out the return trip, so the surviving aircraft were handed over and flown by a Soviet naval mine-torpedo regiment until spare parts ran out in mid-1943. In the game it carries a remarkable load for its size, enough to wipe out over two bases in Air RB, plus the British Mark XII torpedo, which can be released slightly faster than the Soviet 45-36AN. Soviet crews also swapped the dorsal twin Vickers K guns for a single 12.7 mm UBT in a turret. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
hp_12: Handley Page's Type O answered the Royal Navy's call, in Murray Sueter's words, for "a bloody paralyser of an aircraft"; the H.P.12 (O/400) with Eagle VIII engines made up 554 of the 600 built, and the type so impressed the public that "Handley Page" came to mean any huge aeroplane. In the game it climbs, accelerates and holds speed painfully poorly, and its tight turns cost a lot of energy. The Lewis guns fire slowly and cover little, but the airframe soaks up rifle-calibre fire well, and 910 kg of bombs is enough for bases and ground targets. It was a 2025 "The Great War!" event reward, added in the "Hornet's Sting" update.
hs-123a-1: Henschel, better known for building trains, won a 1933 Luftwaffe dive-bomber contest with this all-metal sesquiplane, which flew from the Spanish Civil War until 1944 and was retired only when spare parts ran out. In the game it is a very effective small bomber, carrying either four 50 kg bombs or one 250 kg bomb, backed by two nose-mounted 7.92 mm machine guns with 500 rounds each. Being classed as a bomber gives it an air spawn, a real head start over enemy fighters, and its metal structure tolerates dives up to 577 km/h. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
hs-123a-1_china: China arranged to buy Hs 123 dive bombers from Germany in 1937, but only 12 had arrived by January 1938, and they achieved little before a lack of spares grounded them all in August 1939. The in-game aircraft is essentially the German version in Chinese markings, with only slight performance differences. Its bomb load looks thin, a handful of small bombs or a single larger one, yet accurate drops can destroy most vehicles at its level, and in a pinch it can double as a fighter against lightly protected aircraft. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
hs-129b-2: Henschel's armoured twin-engined attacker was built around engines no other front-line type needed, and the original Argus units left it badly underpowered until captured French Gnome-Rhône 14M radials became available in 1940; even then power was marginal, yet it proved dependable on the Eastern Front and in Tunisia. In the game it is a dedicated tank-hunter: its 30 mm MK 103 or 37 mm BK 3.7 cannons handle light and medium tanks, and its 20 mm guns deal with armoured cars and anti-aircraft vehicles. It is slow and heavy on the controls, but its armour helps it survive, and anything meeting it head-on gets shredded. It has been in the game since the open beta.
hs-129b-2_romania: Romania received an unknown number of Hs 129 B-2s after joining the Axis and used them effectively for ground attack; some pilots even scored air victories in them, Teodor Zăbavă claiming four, and after Romania changed sides in 1944 they were reportedly turned against the Germans. In the game it flies like the standard B-2: slow and ponderous but armoured, with 30 mm or 37 mm cannons for light and medium tanks and 20 mm guns for softer vehicles, though pillboxes and heavy tanks are beyond it. Aircraft that take it on head-on tend to regret it. It was added to the German tree in Update 1.41.
hs-129b-2_romania_italy: The Romanian Air Force flew Hs 129 B-2s with considerable success against ground targets after the country joined the Axis in November 1940, and ace Teodor Zăbavă even shot down four aircraft in one; once Romania switched sides in 1944, the type was reportedly used against its old ally. This Italian-tree copy plays exactly like the German B-2: a sluggish but well-protected tank-buster whose 30 mm and 37 mm cannon options defeat light and medium tanks while 20 mm guns handle lighter vehicles, and whose forward firepower punishes any aircraft attacking it from the front. It arrived in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
hs-129b-3: Faced with ever tougher Soviet tanks, the Germans fitted the Hs 129 with a 75 mm BK 7.5, an airborne adaptation of the PaK 40 anti-tank gun, to strike vulnerable roof armour; 25 were built in August 1944 and worked well even against IS tanks, but there were too few to matter. In the game the "duck" is a pure can-opener: even stock ammunition can penetrate the roof of any tank in the game, though with only 12 rounds every shot has to count. Almost all air-to-air firepower was sacrificed for the gun, and as it is slow and sluggish, enemy fighters find it an easy target. It arrived in Update 1.37.
hudson_mk_v: Developed by Lockheed from its Super Electra airliner, the Hudson served the British Commonwealth in large numbers, some 2,150 aircraft, as a patrol, reconnaissance and light bomber, sinking several German submarines and helping protect Atlantic convoys. In the game it is quick for its rank at around 418 km/h, which matters against the biplanes and early monoplanes it meets, many of which struggle at altitude. The trade-off is a light payload of a few 250 lb bombs and eight solid AP rockets with no explosive filler. Its defensive guns cover the airframe well, but being 7.7 mm weapons they struggle against several attackers at once. It came in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
hunter_f1: Hawker's Hunter grew from a swept-wing development of the Sea Hawk into a single-Avon fighter that first flew in 1951 and joined the RAF in 1954, becoming one of Britain's most successful post-war jets, with nearly 2,000 built and exports to over 20 countries. In the game the F.1 is fast, handles very well at high speed and carries four 30 mm ADEN cannons on a steady gun platform, ideal for diving on unwary targets and leaving before trouble arrives. Low-speed handling is poor, but kept above about 800 km/h it can match F-86s and MiG-17s; supersonic and missile-armed enemies demand more caution. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
hunter_f50_sweden: Sweden bought 120 Hunters as the J34 from 1954 as a stopgap bomber interceptor until the J35 Draken arrived, later adding RB24 missiles; without radar they could only intercept in daylight and clear weather, and the last retired in 1969. In the game it is fast for a subsonic jet, around 1,109 km/h when upgraded, and accelerates well above 700 km/h. Its four ADEN cannons kill most aircraft in a short burst, the RB24s suit distracted or slow targets, and it holds energy well enough to energy-trap delta-wings like the MiG-21. Below 700 km/h it handles badly, and it has no countermeasures. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
hunter_f58_switzerland: Serial J-4020 flew with the Patrouille Suisse display team, one of the Swiss Air Force's Hunter F.58s, which the KAWEST upgrade gave a radar warning receiver, ECM pod, chaff and the ability to fire AIM-9s and AGM-65Bs; the airframe is now displayed at Dübendorf near Zurich. Those upgrades set it apart from the British F.6 and FGA.9 in the game: it carries AIM-9P and AGM-65B missiles plus RWR and countermeasures. Opponents are often supersonic and missile-armed, but its ADEN cannons and Sidewinders punish anyone low on energy or inattentive, and good energy retention helps it slip away. A German-tree squadron vehicle, it came in the "Sky Guardians" update and introduced Switzerland to the game.
hunter_f58a_1971_switzerland: After its own FFA P-16 fighter project failed, Switzerland turned to the Hunter, ordering 100 in 1958; in 1971 it added 52 more built to FGA.9 standard as the F.58A, delivered in parts and assembled at Emmen with Sidewinder provisions and an improved Avon 207 engine. In the game it keeps energy well and hits hard with its cannons, backed by two air-to-air missiles, while the usual Hunter weakness of limited manoeuvrability remains. Its main difference from the British FGA.9 lies in the weapons it can carry under the wings. It joined the German tree in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
hunter_f6: The F.6 fixed the early Hunters' short range and gun-induced compressor stalls with a bigger engine, revised wing and more fuel, and led RAF fighter squadrons until the Lightning took over from 1963; one tested the SRAAM missile, groundwork for the later ASRAAM. In the game it adds power to the F.1's strong high-speed handling, energy retention and 30 mm ADEN cannons. Its signature weapon is the SRAAM, a thrust-vectoring missile that can hit from almost any angle but only within about 1 km and is easily fooled by flares. Without an afterburner it is slower than most contemporaries, and it has no radar, RWR or countermeasures. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
hunter_f6_holland: The Royal Netherlands Air Force ordered Hunters in 1955 to replace its ageing piston and early jet fighters; Fokker licence-built F.4s and T.7 trainers, while the 93 F.6s came straight from British production and served until the F-104G Starfighter took over in 1968. In the game it is a hard-hitting fighter that conserves energy well, though its turning is only average and supersonic opponents outpace it. The difference from the British F.6 lies in its underwing weapons, limited to AIM-9B Sidewinders. It joined the French tree in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
hunter_f9_rhodesia: The FGA.9 adapted the Hunter F.6 for ground attack with improved hydraulic controls; Rhodesia flew it through the Bush War, and Zimbabwe used it into the Second Congo War and still keeps at least two. In the game an uprated engine and AIM-9E missiles make it one of the best Hunters, second only to the Swiss F.58. It excels at energy fighting for an alert pilot, lacking countermeasures against missiles such as the AIM-9L or R-60M, and heavy bombs and rockets make it a strong striker. A premium pack from Update 1.93 "Shark Attack", it was withdrawn following the 9th Anniversary Sale and has returned only briefly, in 2022 and 2023.
hurricane_mk1: Hawker's Hurricane brought a Merlin engine and retractable undercarriage to RAF squadrons in 1937 and was credited with 60% of the Luftwaffe's losses during the Battle of Britain; the late Mk I gained metal-covered wings, a three-blade metal propeller, cockpit armour and self-sealing tanks, with around 500 built. In the game it lacks the Spitfire's speed and agility but is a capable all-rounder that keeps pace with most opponents and shrugs off hits from rifle-calibre guns. Its energy retention is only average, which can leave it exposed once the fight slows down. It has been in the game since the open beta.
hurricane_mk1_late_ep: A cosmetic variant of the late Mk I Hurricane, the FAA M wears the camouflage of Fleet Air Arm training aircraft and was added to mark the 80th anniversary of the Battle of Britain; otherwise it matches the standard Mk I/L, which Sydney Camm's team improved with metal-covered wings, armour and a three-bladed variable-pitch propeller. With plenty of ammunition and excellent manoeuvrability it is at home in turning fights with enemy fighters. It is slow, though, struggling to catch some opponents, more so at altitude, and its 7.7 mm guns lack the punch for bombers or armoured targets.
hurricane_mk1_late_finland: Finland's Hurricane Mk I/Ls were bought in 1940, but a shortage of spare parts meant they saw only limited use in the Continuation War; this one now sits in the Swedish tree. It cannot quite match a Spitfire for speed or agility, but by the standards of its rank it turns well and dogfights effectively. Its real strengths are toughness, as the largely fabric-covered airframe absorbs a great deal of punishment, and a steady gun platform that makes aiming easy, which together make it a forgiving choice for newer pilots. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
hurricane_mk1b: Built for carrier service, the Sea Hurricane Mk IB is the naval counterpart of the Hurricane Mk I/L, operating from flight decks as well as runways thanks to strengthened landing gear. That extra weight is its main drawback: in Realistic and Simulator battles it climbs and turns noticeably worse and needs more speed to take off, though the difference is minor in Arcade. The added mass does improve dive acceleration, so boom-and-zoom attacks work better than on the land-based version, provided the pilot can first gain the height. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
hurricane_mk1c: The Fleet Air Arm found the Sea Hurricane Mk IB short on endurance and firepower, and its answer was the Mk IC, with four 20 mm Hispano cannons; from January 1942 these conversions of combat-worn land Hurricanes, combining old fuselages with new wings and engines, flew from the carriers Eagle, Furious and Victorious, and the last were retired in April 1944. In the game it is an agile carrier fighter with heavy firepower. Its weaknesses are low speed, sluggish acceleration and controls that stiffen quickly in a dive. It came in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
hurricane_mk4: The Mk IV was the Hurricane reworked as a dedicated attack aircraft, with extra armour around the engine and cockpit and the ability to carry RP-3 rockets, 500 lb bombs or a pair of 40 mm Vickers S cannons, leaving just one machine gun per wing; 524 were built between 1942 and 1944. In the game it turns even better than earlier Hurricanes, but its job is destroying tanks and ships. It climbs poorly and bleeds energy in dogfights, its 7.7 mm guns are weak, and the 40 mm cannons kick hard and hold only 15 rounds each, so air combat is best left to others. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
hurricanemkii: A tropicalised Hurricane Mk II, the IIB carried twelve 7.7 mm machine guns plus bomb racks, the extra guns preferred because the RAF still distrusted the jam-prone Hispano cannon; it found its real niche attacking ground targets in North Africa, leaving air fighting to the Spitfire. In the game the extra weight makes it slower and less lively than the Mk I, though it is still agile enough to fight, held back mainly by speed and acceleration. Twelve guns with a huge ammunition supply tear apart fabric biplanes, leave plenty for ground targets and can batter sturdier monoplanes in uptiers. It has been in the game since the open beta.
hurricanemkii_ussr: This premium Hurricane Mk IIB is a Lend-Lease aircraft re-armed in Soviet service with two 20 mm ShVAK cannons and 12.7 mm Berezin UB machine guns, giving it heavier firepower than the British original. That punch, combined with the Hurricane's tight turning, makes it dangerous in a close dogfight. The airframe's performance lags behind its contemporaries, however, so getting into a favourable position takes some work. It is a sturdy, hard-hitting turn-fighter that arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
i-153_m62: The Chaika extended the I-15 line after the Spanish Civil War persuaded Soviet planners that an updated biplane still had a role, adding retractable landing gear, rapid-firing ShKAS guns and a gull-shaped upper wing; it held its own against the Ki-27 at Khalkhin Gol but suffered from unreliable engines and fuel fires before being relegated to light attack. In the game it is arguably the finest biplane fighter of all, out-turning and out-rolling any monoplane, with very fast-firing guns and useful ground-attack options. Like any biplane it is slow and fragile, so a pilot who loses track of the fight will quickly be caught. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-153_m62_china: Among the 1,250 Soviet aircraft sent to China between 1937 and 1941 were 93 I-153s, delivered in 1940 and organised into three groups defending major cities, where most were lost fighting Japanese fighters and bombers. Polikarpov's Chaika had brought back the gull-shaped upper wing and added retractable gear, a more powerful M-62 engine and pilot armour. In the game it is outstanding in a turn, with respectable speed and climb for a biplane, and can carry rockets or bombs alongside its four light ShKAS guns. It is fragile, though, and monoplanes outrun it both in level flight and in a dive. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
i-153_m62_zhukovskiy: Sergey Zhukovsky became an ace in a single day on 22 June 1941, scoring five kills over nine sorties in his I-153 as Germany invaded the Soviet Union; he ended the war with 28 victories, 13 of them personal, and this aircraft wears the white scheme of his Chaika. In the game it is one of the very best biplanes, able to out-turn and out-roll every monoplane and armed with rapid-firing ShKAS machine guns, and it can attack ground targets as well as aircraft. The usual biplane failings, low speed and a fragile airframe, punish any pilot who loses track of the sky around them. It arrived in Update 1.31.
i-153p: A premium Chaika armed with two 20 mm cannons, the I-153P can out-turn every aircraft it meets, and many opponents underestimate it and try to turn with it anyway, usually to their cost. Its weaknesses are just as stark: nearly everything it faces is faster, its controls stiffen badly at high speed, and the airframe is so fragile that a single 20 mm hit is usually fatal. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-15_1934: Polikarpov's I-15 refined the I-5 and I-6 into a gull-winged biplane with an open cockpit and fixed undercarriage, first flown by V. P. Chkalov in October 1934; this WR version used an imported Wright Cyclone, kept as delivered on the first 50 aircraft and modified on later ones, notably in the gun synchronisation gear. It carried two 7.62 mm PV-1 machine guns, an aircraft version of the Maxim, with 750 rounds each, and an optical sight derived from the British Aldis. Small bombs could go under the lower wing; in the game it can take a pair of 50 kg FAB-50s. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-15_1935: Polikarpov's I-15 went into 1935 production at a time when licence-building of the Wright Cyclone as the M-25 was lagging, so most aircraft received the M-22 instead, a licensed Bristol Jupiter VI derivative of only 480 hp that held back their performance. Later production I-15s did get the M-25, but this version keeps the weaker engine, with one consolation: it is 153 kg lighter than the M-25 model. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-15_1935_moscow: The I-15 M-25 represents Polikarpov's biplane fitted with the M-25, the Soviet licence-built Wright Cyclone, whose slow introduction meant most I-15s of 1935 had to make do with the 480 hp M-22 instead. In the game the stronger engine makes it the better of the two versions, outperforming the I-15 M-22. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-15bis: The I-15bis entered Soviet service in late 1937 and, with 2,408 built by the end of 1939, was the second most common member of the I-15 family after the I-153. In China it got the better of the Ki-10 biplane but had a hard time against monoplanes like the A5M and Ki-27, and once the Zero and Bf 109 appeared it was soon pushed into ground attack. In the game it serves as a straightforward first fighter for its line, relying on agility and doing best when it draws opponents into fights it can win. It arrived in Update 1.31.
i-15bis_china: China received 347 I-15bis fighters from the Soviet Union from 1937 and flew them until 1940, with their best results coming in the defence of Wuhan against Japanese bombers; Chinese units also pioneered pairing the agile I-15bis with faster I-16s. In the game it is built for fighting other aircraft: it turns superbly, and its forward guns with incendiary belts readily ignite biplanes and early monoplanes. Low speed and a fragile airframe are the price. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
i-15bis_krasnolutsky: This I-15bis carries the camouflage of Mitrofan Krasnolutsky, a squadron commander in the 65th ShAP who, on 12 August 1941, rammed a Finnish MS.406 with his biplane; remarkably, both aircraft made it home with damaged wings. He was later made a Hero of the Soviet Union and rose to major general. Beyond the paint scheme it matches the regular I-15bis, combining excellent agility and good forward firepower with low speed and poor survivability. It arrived in Update 2.25 "Sky Guardians".
i-16_chung_28: The Chung 28 was China's attempt at building its own fighters during the war with Japan: in caves near Chongqing, the relocated Central Aircraft Factory assembled I-16s from Soviet spare parts and paired them with American piston engines. Outclassed almost immediately, they ended up training new pilots and were probably scrapped by the war's end. In the game it flies as well as the late-production I-16s but carries only two 7.62 mm machine guns, so saving ammunition for close-range shots is essential; flown that way, it can still catch out more modern fighters. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
i-16_type10: The type 10 doubled the I-16's firepower to four ShKAS machine guns, two of them in the cowling, which makes convergence settings less critical than on the wing-gunned type 5, though a close setting of 150–400 m still works best. Having four guns also means a jam from overheating costs only a quarter of its firepower, and a PAK-1 reflector sight replaces the earlier telescopic sight, easing close-range aiming. It remains an unsteady gun platform without trim control, however. Six RS-82 rockets can be fitted, but they are unreliable against armour and only worth carrying in specific situations. It arrived in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
i-16_type10_china: Built in 1938–39 with an M-25V engine, a new gunsight and a doubled armament of four ShKAS machine guns, the type 10 reached China from spring 1938, where it proved valuable against Japanese bombing raids even if newer Japanese fighters outclassed it. In the game only biplanes and Japanese fighters can match its agility, and with decent guns and a good climb rate it handles both turning fights and hit-and-run attacks. A thin 6 mm armour plate offers little protection, though, and its modest top speed shows most against German fighters. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
i-16_type17_china: The type 17 replaced the I-16's wing machine guns with 20 mm ShVAK cannons; 341 were built, and China bought 75 in early 1941, only to find them outmatched by the A6M Zero. In the game the cannons and good agility make it a strong dogfighter, and its underwing weapons can deal with ground targets if aimed carefully. Speed and climb are below par for a fighter, which matters most against Bf 109s, and its 8.5 mm armour plate gives scant protection. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
i-16_type18: Nicknamed "Ishak", the I-16 was the emblem of the pre-war Soviet air force and remained its main fighter until 1942, though it was outdated by 1941 and soon gave way to the Yak-1 and La-5. The type 18, developed during the fighting at Khalkhin Gol, swapped the type 10's engine for the M-62 also used in the I-153. In the game it is very agile, with respectable guns and underwing weapons, but it is slow and does not take much punishment. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-16_type24: The type 24 of 1939 stiffened the I-16's wings with plywood skin between the spars, strengthened the airframe and adopted the M-63 engine; it fought at Khalkhin Gol, in Poland and in the Winter War, and despite being dated served widely in the early months of the war with Germany. In the game its agility is matched only by a few Japanese fighters, and with good guns it makes a capable dogfighter. Protection is limited to an armoured seat back, and the M-63 overheats quickly. It arrived in Update 1.39.
i-16_type27: Polikarpov's I-16 is credited as the first low-wing cantilever monoplane fighter with a retractable undercarriage to become operational, and in Spain it outclassed biplanes like the He 51 and CR.32 until the Bf 109 arrived. The type 27 combined the type 17's armament, two nose ShKAS and two wing-mounted ShVAK cannons, with the M-62 engine. In the game it has the best weapon and ordnance options of any I-16 and out-turns nearly everything except the likes of the A6M and Spitfire, making it a dangerous opponent for its size. Its weaknesses are low top speed, which makes many targets hard to catch, and a poor dive limit. It arrived in Update 1.39.
i-16_type28: The type 28 paired the M-63 engine of the type 24 with wing-mounted ShVAK cannons; just over a hundred were built and flew at Khalkhin Gol and during the war with Germany. In the game it is practically the same as the type 27: underwing weapons let it attack ground targets, even armoured vehicles, but it is really at home in dogfights, where its agility, good firepower and decent climb rate count. A 6 mm armour plate offers little protection, and German fighters in particular will easily outpace it in level flight. It has been in the game since the open beta.
i-16_type5: Developed in 1935 from the type 4 with a stronger M-25A engine and minor structural changes, the I-16 type 5 was built in large numbers, 2,895 by 1937, and fought at Lake Khasan, at Khalkhin Gol, in Spain, in China and into the war with Germany. In the game only a few Japanese fighters can turn with it, and with decent guns and a good climb rate it suits both close dogfights and hit-and-run passes. The price of that agility is fragility: there is no armour at all, and the M-25A overheats easily. It arrived in Update 1.43.
i-16_type5_1935_china: Chiang Kai-shek's China received I-16 type 5s from the Soviet Union during the war with Japan, and they fought in the Battle of Nanjing; the type was a 1935 update of the type 4 with a stronger M-25A engine, and 2,895 were built. The Chinese aircraft plays just like the Soviet one: very few aircraft, mainly some Japanese fighters, can turn with it, and decent guns plus a good climb rate let it either dogfight or strike and extend. There is no armour, however, and the engine is quick to overheat. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
i_180: Polikarpov's I-180S aimed to build a more powerful radial-engined interceptor on the basis of the I-16, but engine and propeller troubles and the death of a test pilot dogged its development, and its cancellation has been blamed partly on politics. In the game it looks like an I-16 and flies like a faster one, with excellent top speed, climb and turning, if ordinary acceleration. Two 12.7 mm BS and two ShKAS guns are light next to the cannon-armed fighters it meets, but its performance gets it into good positions early and up to high-flying bombers. It was the 2019 "Battlefield Engineer" event reward, added in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
i_185_m71_standard: This I-185 pairs the Shvetsov M-71 radial with three fuselage-mounted 20 mm ShVAK cannons, carrying 140, 170 and 250 rounds respectively, and protects its fuel with self-sealing tanks in the fuselage and wings. In the game it is a dedicated boom-and-zoom fighter: it has to keep its energy high at all times to hunt effectively, diving on targets and climbing back rather than settling into turning fights. It arrived in Update 1.41.
i_185_m82: With the M-82 radial, the I-185 can be seen as a Soviet counterpart to the Fw 190: its roll rate, climb and dive acceleration all favour boom-and-zoom attacks. Like many Yaks, though, it has no single standout trait, and while it is a strong energy fighter it is really a jack-of-all-trades. High-altitude performance is weak, as with most Soviet fighters, even if it can operate somewhat higher than the Yaks. It arrived in Update 1.37.
i_225: The I-225 closed out the I-220 line of high-altitude interceptors derived from the MiG-3, the heaviest and most powerful of the series, with a pressurised cockpit, seat armour and four 20 mm ShVAK cannons; the second prototype, the one modelled in the game, was the second-fastest Soviet piston fighter after the Yak-3M, but work on the I-250 left it sidelined. In the game it is among the best Soviet propeller fighters and truly comes alive at high altitude, outperforming most rivals there. Diving into low-level fights is riskier, because its controls stiffen at high speed. It arrived in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
i_29: A premium gift aircraft, the I-29 is a fast twin-engined heavy fighter from the Yakovlev design bureau, developed before the war and incorporating many promising ideas. It was first given out in Update 1.73 "Vive la France" to mark War Thunder's fifth anniversary, and returned as one of the prizes in the "10 rare vehicles" event celebrating the game's tenth anniversary in 2022.
ia_58a_pucara: Argentina's twin-turboprop Pucará counter-insurgency aircraft first flew in 1969, and in the 1982 Falklands War its short-field ability made it the only Argentine combat type able to fly from the islands themselves; 19 were lost and five captured, but a pair of them scored Argentina's sole air-to-air kill of the conflict by downing a Scout helicopter at Goose Green. In the game it carries heavy armament, gets a useful boost from its water-injected WEP and can use JATO boosters. Without flaps deployed it becomes much less agile, though, and the WEP boost runs out quickly. It joined the German tree in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
iar_316b: Romania licence-built the Alouette III as the IAR 316B at Brașov from 1971 to 1987, fitting it for Soviet-bloc rockets, guns and anti-tank missiles; half of the 250 built served at home, and the others were exported to countries such as Pakistan, Angola and Guinea. In the game it resembles the French SA 316B but has extra options: machine guns for air-to-air use, plus Malyutka-2 ATGMs and S-5K rockets against ground targets. It is quick and agile but unarmoured, so careful flying is needed to survive. It was sold as a premium pack from Update 1.87 "Locked On" until the 2019 Birthday Sale.
iar_81c: Romania's IAR-80 drew on the Polish PZL P.24 and a licence-built Gnome-Rhône radial, outperformed the He 112 in 1939 trials and became the country's main fighter, with about 450 of the family built; the IAR-81C was the most advanced version, with two 20 mm MG 151/20 cannons and two machine guns, and helped defend the Ploiești oil fields against American raids. In the game its speed, climb and agility are all middling, so tactics must be tailored to each opponent, but the twin cannons can bring down even sturdy aircraft, and bombs or rockets give it a role against ground targets in combined battles. It joined the Italian tree in Update 1.79 "Project X".
iar_81c_db_605: Looking for more power than the IAR-80 family's own engine could give, Romania first tried a DB 601 in 1941, with alarming vibration, then in mid-1943 fitted a DB 605 A to IAR-81C airframe No. 326; it flew excellently, but Germany could not spare the engines and Romania could not build enough, so it never entered production. In the game the far stronger engine transforms the IAR-81C, bringing much higher speed, better energy retention and a greatly improved climb, although agility stays average. Its 20 mm cannons remain deadly against any aircraft, and rockets or 50 kg bombs handle lightly armoured ground targets. It was the reward for Battle Pass Season XXIV, "Do It Yourself".
iar_93b: Romania and Yugoslavia agreed in 1971 to build a simple, rugged subsonic attack jet together, and both prototypes flew on the same day in October 1974; the IAR-93B improved on the A with a new wing, extra hardpoints, bigger fuel tanks and cleaner aerodynamics, and 34 were built, serving until 1998. In the game it is a capable attacker with a ballistic computer, a radar warning receiver, short-range missiles to protect itself in a dogfight and good handling. It lacks countermeasures, though, and most other jets it meets are faster. It was a 2024 "Flight of the Vulture" event reward, made through the Revenue Share programme for the Italian tree.
il-10: Ilyushin turned its abandoned IL-1 light fighter-attacker into a sleeker, faster successor to the IL-2, and it beat Sukhoi's Su-6 for the job thanks to better speed and agility despite carrying less; production aircraft saw action in the closing phase of the war in Europe. This 1945 version keeps the Sturmovik's weapons: a pair of 23 mm VYa-23 cannons and two ShKAS forward, plus a 12.7 mm Berezin for the gunner. In the game it is much quicker than the IL-2M but most opposing fighters still outpace it; it does retain its predecessor's agility, which a pilot who manages energy carefully can exploit in air combat. It arrived in Update 1.41.
il-10_1946: The post-war IL-10 swapped the Sturmovik's VYa cannons for four wing-mounted 23 mm NS-23s, which are deadly against aircraft of any size but penetrate much less armour, and gave the rear gunner a 20 mm B-20 cannon in place of a machine gun. In the game it is a dangerous opponent in slow, low-altitude dogfights, while armour around the cockpit and engine helps against small-calibre AP rounds. Higher up and at speed, late piston fighters such as the F8F-1B hold the advantage, and its weight blunts acceleration. The cannon shells are slow, so careful leading is essential; an air-targets belt serves well against both aircraft and light ground targets. It arrived in Update 1.41.
il-10_1946_china: The Soviet Union supplied 242 IL-10s to the young PLAAF in the early 1950s; once crews had gained experience they fought Nationalist forces on the offshore islands from 1954, suppressing air defences on the Dachen Islands ahead of Tu-2 bombing raids and later sinking a landing ship off Yijiangshan. Two were even re-engined with WJ-6 turboprops, though both were lost in accidents, and the type served until the Q-5 replaced it in 1972. The in-game aircraft matches the Soviet IL-10 (1946), combining four 23 mm cannons and a useful bomb load for ground attack with a cannon-armed rear gunner that discourages pursuit. It joined the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
il-10_1946_hungary: Hungary received about 160 IL-10s between 1949 and 1952, some from the Soviet Union and others built under licence in Czechoslovakia as the B-33, and flew them with three assault regiments until August 1956, when MiG-15s took their place. The IL-10 itself, first flown in 1944, had been designed to cure the IL-2's lack of speed. In the game its heavy armament and respectable bomb load make it well suited to mixed battles, though speed and agility are unremarkable next to its main opponents and it climbs slowly. It joined the Italian tree in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
il-2i: Once the 23 mm VYa-23 cannon originally intended for the IL-2 was ready, one early aircraft was fitted with a pair and tried as the IL-2I, a heavy interceptor for hunting German bombers; it proved too slow for that, so VYa-armed IL-2s went back to ground attack. In the game, where it appears as the IL-2 (1942), those two cannons hit hard against aircraft and ground targets alike. Like other Sturmoviks it is tough and slow, but its sharp initial turn can surprise attackers who get careless. It has been in the game since the aircraft closed beta test.
il-2m: The IL-2M type 3, or KSW, countered the two-seat IL-2's rearward centre of gravity by sweeping the wing leading edges back 15 degrees, and from autumn 1943 most had metal instead of wooden wings. In the game its armour shields pilot and engine from small-calibre fire, and the airframe shrugs off even heavy machine gun and cannon hits. Generous ordnance and strong forward guns make it a serious threat to tanks and a fearsome head-on attacker, while the rear gunner gives pursuers something to worry about. Mediocre flight performance means it rarely escapes fighters by speed. It has been in the game since the closed beta.
il-2m_mstitel: Sold as a premium version of the IL-2M type 3 from Update 1.41.27, the "Avenger" left the store after the 2016 clearance sale and has since returned only briefly, in the 2018 Winter Sale and for Golden Eagles during several "Defender of the Fatherland" events and the 2023 "Defender Special". In the game it is heavily armoured but sluggish and quick to lose energy, so fighters are best avoided. Its 23 mm cannons can wreck any aircraft they hit, yet turning fights are a job for real fighters, and a 12.7 mm UB in the rear guards its tail.
il-4: Ilyushin's twin-engined IL-4 served the Soviet air force as a front-line and occasionally long-range bomber, and the navy as a torpedo bomber carrying the 45-36AN; with a four-man crew, a range of over 2,000 km and up to 2,000 kg of bombs, it stayed in use until 1949 after its intended successor, the IL-6, was cancelled. In the game it handles much like the DB-3B before it, differing mainly in engines and defensive guns, and its varied payloads make it useful in air, ground and naval battles alike. Speed and agility are limited compared with fighters or light bombers. It has been in the game since the open beta.
il_28: Drawing on lessons from captured German jet designs, Ilyushin's IL-28 exceeded the Soviet Union's 1948 requirement for a jet front-line bomber once it received VK-1 engines, and it became a fixture of Eastern Bloc air forces and many export users; China built it as the H-5, and North Korea still had around 80 in 2023. In the game it continues the fast-bomber tradition of aircraft like the Pe-2, with better flight performance than most of its class, letting it slip away from threats. A twin NR-23 tail turret guards the rear, and two more NR-23s in the nose let the pilot pick off light ground targets or careless aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.43.
il_28_china: When worsening relations with Moscow ruled out importing a production line, Harbin reverse-engineered the IL-28, lightening it and adapting it to Chinese manufacturing; the resulting H-5 first flew in 1966, and 507 served with the PLAAF, a few being passed to Albania and North Korea, until the type was retired by 2009. In the game it is close to the Soviet IL-28 in looks and performance, combining a broad choice of payloads with enough speed to leave the battlefield quickly. Its 23 mm defensive cannons can bring down pursuing jets in one burst, but enemies with air-to-air missiles can kill it from beyond their reach. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
il_28_german: East Germany's air force operated 13 IL-28s, including one IL-28U trainer, but used them mainly for towing targets and testing engines rather than bombing, since its bomber units flew other types. In the game it is the same as the Soviet IL-28 and continues the German tree's line of fast front-line bombers after the Do 217 and Ar 234: dash in, hit one target accurately and leave before fighters can respond. A generous air spawn and strong tail guns help it do exactly that, and it is good practice for later strike aircraft such as the MiG-23BN. It arrived in the "Raining Fire" update.
il_28_hungary: Hungary obtained IL-28s from the Soviet Union in the late 1950s and flew them through the Cold War until the Su-22M3 took over their strike role; this one wears the markings of aircraft No. 55, now preserved at the aviation museum in Szolnok. It behaves exactly like the Soviet IL-28, carrying on the Italian tree's fast-bomber role from the piston-engined Tu-2S-59: get in quickly, strike precisely and escape before interceptors arrive, aided by its air spawn and capable tail guns. It joined the game in the "Alpha Strike" update and leads on to the Su-22M3.
il_28sh: The IL-28Sh added twelve underwing pylons to turn the bomber into a ground-attack aircraft, but trials from autumn 1967 showed that its large size, thin armour and lack of ejection seats usable at low altitude made the role too dangerous, and only a handful of the 300 planned conversions were completed before the effort moved on to a purpose-built attacker. In the game its extra stores, including additional cannons, rockets and incendiary bombs, make it devastating in combined battles, provided it lives long enough to use them. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
il_2_1941: With 36,183 built across all versions, the IL-2 is the most-produced military aircraft ever, and its role name, Sturmovik, became its nickname; designed around an armoured cockpit and the 23 mm VYa-23 cannon, it was overweight and underpowered but proved surprisingly agile and hard to kill. This earliest production model, the first Sturmovik in the Soviet tree, has no rear gunner and makes do with two 20 mm ShVAK cannons, weaker than the later VYa-23 but still adequate against most aircraft it meets. It is tough, slow and somewhat clumsy, yet its unexpectedly good turn can catch attackers out. It arrived in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
il_2_1942_luftwaffe: One single-seat IL-2 of 1942, callsign "Red-White 4", fell into German hands on the Eastern Front and was repainted in Luftwaffe markings with yellow bands; it was probably flown on ground-attack sorties only until the captured ammunition ran out. The type itself, with more than 36,000 built, remains the most-produced military aircraft ever, and this simplified 1942 version lacked a rear gunner. Within Germany's line-up it is unusually tough, able to do real damage to ground forces and still look after itself against fighters. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
il_2_37_1943: Of all the two-seat IL-2s, the IL-2-37 is the slowest, so it has no business anywhere but the ground-attack role; trying anything else tends to end quickly. Its purpose is tank-busting with a pair of NS-37 cannons, and it does that job reasonably well, especially when diving steeply to hit the roof of a tank, where shots can start fires or knock out the crew. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
il_2_m82: As German advances in 1941 threatened production of the IL-2's AM-38 engine, Ilyushin proposed fitting the air-cooled M-82 radial and a second crew seat; a single prototype was built, but once AM-38 output resumed in 1942 the work was dropped, and it never saw combat. In the game it shares the IL-2 family's tough, well-armoured construction, and its rockets and bombs are effective against armoured vehicles. It is slow and climbs poorly, however, and its weak point is the M-82 itself, which has no armour and is easily put out of action. It was a reward in World War mode season 3, "Road to the West".
il_2m_1943: Built from late 1942 to the end of 1943, the IL-2M (1943) gained the AM-38F engine, which ran faster, offered a ten-minute boost mode and restored a bomb load of around 600 kg, though it still ran hot like its predecessors. In the game it carries two 23 mm VYa-23 cannons with 150 rounds each and two ShKAS machine guns, and the armoured-target belt's AP rounds can punch through as much as 46 mm of armour. A 12.7 mm gun behind the pilot defends the rear, but its arcs are limited, particularly downwards. Varied ordnance makes it a capable ground attacker. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
il_8_1944: In 1942 Ilyushin was asked for two IL-2 successors: the IL-10, which traded payload for performance, and the IL-8, which went the other way with heavier armour and a 1,000 kg load. Both used the troublesome AM-42 engine, and although the IL-8's armoured version completed its trials in spring 1944, the IL-10's success kept it out of production. In the game a respectable bomb load and strong protection make it well suited to mixed battles, but it has no rockets, and while it outpaces the IL-2 at every altitude, fighters are still far faster. It was the reward for Battle Pass season 14, "Airborne General".
il_9a33bm3: Greece acquired much of the former East German army's equipment after reunification, with deliveries between 1992 and 1994 including Osa-AKM air-defence systems; 38 were still in Greek service in 2024, when some were sold to Armenia. In the Israeli tree it performs exactly like the Soviet Osa-AKM, able to hit manoeuvring aircraft out to 10 km and to guide two missiles onto one target at once.
