Its wheeled chassis makes it quick to reposition and spring surprises on aircraft, but it is large, essentially unarmoured, and its upward-angled launchers make it almost useless against ground vehicles. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
il_aml_90: Panhard's AML-90 swapped the mortar of the earlier AML-60 for a low-pressure 90 mm gun firing HE and HEAT shells, and Israel bought around 23 from France in the early 1960s, using them in the Six-Day and Yom Kippur Wars. In the game its 90 mm gun penetrates well and reloads reasonably quickly, but the armour stops almost nothing, not even .50 calibre fire, so survival depends on speed and good positioning. It is best used for flanking, harassing the enemy, capturing points and supporting teammates, ideally on flat ground, since its wheels can get stuck in rough terrain. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_amx_13_75: Israel bought 400 AMX-13s from France between 1956 and 1967 and, lacking modern main battle tanks because of arms embargoes, sent them into the front line in the Six-Day War instead of scouting; heavy losses followed and they were soon retired. In the game it can use speed and agility to flank heavier tanks or snipe from medium to long range at weaker ones. It fires only solid APCBC shot with no explosive filler, so one-shot kills are rare; targeting the gunner or barrel and exploiting the 5-second autoloader works better. Like most light tanks, it is easily ambushed in towns. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_centurion_mk_5_shot: Sho't, Hebrew for "whip", was Israel's name for the Centurion Mk.5, received from Britain between 1958 and 1960 to replace Shermans that could not match the M48s and T-54s fielded by Arab armies; it performed well and proved survivable in the 1967 Six-Day War. In the game it is identical to the Centurion Mk.5/1. Its strength is neither speed, armour nor raw penetration, as its 84 mm gun trails weapons like the T-54's D-10T, but gun handling: a two-axis stabiliser and capable APDS let it fire on the move, push around corners and react to surprises without stopping. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_centurion_shot_kal_alef: After 1967 the Sho't's 20-pounder, dated fire control and thirsty, weak engine were clearly inadequate, so from 1970 Israel rebuilt its Centurions as the Sho't Kal with the American 105 mm M68, a stronger diesel and new fire control; the Alef was the first such standard and fought in the 1973 Yom Kippur War. In the game its Continental AVDS-1790-2A diesel gives a mobility boost similar to the Centurion Mk 10 and Strv 101, and the M68 adds stronger HEATFS and HESH rounds. The original Mk.5 hull still protects poorly, leaving it exposed even to APCR and solid shot. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_centurion_shot_kal_d: The Sho't Kal Dalet of 1984 was the last production version of Israel's upgraded Centurion, adding the Barak Or fire control and better-placed Blazer reactive armour; Merkavas had fully replaced it by 1992, though it trained crews until 2002. In the game it is close to the Sho't Kal Gimel but has outstanding fire control for its rank, including a thermal sight that can see through foliage. With a 105 mm gun firing HEATFS and APFSDS, it is a dangerous shooter. Acceleration is sluggish, though, and the side armour stops little more than heavy machine gun fire. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
il_centurion_shot_kal_gimel: The third production upgrade of Israel's Centurion-based Sho't Kal appeared between the late 1970s and early 1980s, adding extra machine guns, ten-round smoke launchers on the turret sides and Blazer reactive armour on hull and turret; it left service with the other Sho't Kals in 2007. In the game it improves on earlier Sho't Kals with a laser rangefinder, smoke grenades and the potent M111 "Hetz" round, while the ERA blocks offer welcome protection against HEAT shells and ATGMs, which become common at this rank. It keeps good mobility and very useful gun depression, but lacks the thermal sight of the later Dalet. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_eitan: Developed by Israel's Mantak to replace the ageing M113 and named after Operation Protective Edge, the wheeled Eitan entered production as an AFV in 2022, while this IFV version with a 30 mm Bushmaster II, Spike missiles and Iron Fist active protection remained a single prototype. In the game it is big and fairly quick, protected by side ERA, thin composite panels in front and an Iron Fist system that defeats most ATGMs and HEAT shells. Cannon and Spikes let it tackle anything from light vehicles to tanks. The crew is packed into the nose, the turret sits awkwardly far back, and the armour is no match for a tank's. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
il_hunter_afv: Singapore's Hunter replaced the army's ageing M113 Ultras; developed from 2006 and built by ST Kinetics, it was unveiled in 2018 and entered service from 2019, with all weapons operated remotely from inside the hull and electronic systems giving the crew all-round awareness. In the Israeli tree its remotely operated turret pairs a 30 mm cannon with two Spike missiles, and the vehicle moves quickly both forwards and in reverse. Its armour, however, can be defeated by autocannons, and its large size makes it an easy target. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
il_leopard_2a6_hel: After a 1998 tank competition Greece chose the Leopard 2 and in 2003 settled on an upgraded 2A6, the 2HEL, with 30 built in Germany and 140 assembled locally; it entered service in 2008 and now forms the core of Greek armour. In the game its distinguishing feature is extra composite armour on the hull front, like that of the Leopard 2A7V and Strv 122, and it can wear camouflage netting. Beyond that it is a standard late Leopard 2 with a 120 mm L/55 gun, potent APFSDS and modern thermals. Gun movement is restricted when aiming over the rear and sides, and an ammunition rack sits beside the driver. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
il_m109: Israel fielded the M109 self-propelled howitzer from the late 1960s, using it to strike key enemy positions in the 1973 Yom Kippur War and again in Lebanon in 1982, before longer-ranged versions replaced the early vehicles by 2006. In the game its 155 mm HE shell is very powerful, and the short-barrelled gun, while not suited to long-range shooting, is easy to use even for beginners. It works best in support, flanking or waiting in cover to ambush, aiming at turret roofs, lower hulls or engine decks, because the shell cannot reliably defeat Cold War tanks from the front. It arrived in the "Kings of Battle" update.
il_m109a1: Rochev was the IDF name for its M109 howitzers up to the M109A2, which differed mostly internally; by 2006 only the long-barrelled M185 version remained, often with field additions such as extra machine guns and stowage boxes. In the game it is a modest upgrade on the regular M109: the M185 fires the same 155 mm shells with no extra penetration, but higher velocity makes long shots easier. A barrel-mounted 7.62 mm machine gun clears obstacles, hits unarmoured targets and helps with ranging. Thin armour and a slow reload make it fragile, but a well-placed HE shell can still kill most MBTs. It arrived in the "Air Superiority" update.
il_m113_hvms: Bardelas is Israel's name for the M113, which it operated in huge numbers, up to 6,000 at a time; this version mounts the 60 mm HVMS gun, developed by Israel after a joint project with OTO Melara split in two, and offered for several vehicles including the M113, though only Chile ever bought it, for its M24s and M50s. In the game the gun hits reasonably hard but penetrates poorly and is slow to reload for its calibre, and its aiming angles are limited and often blocked by fittings on the roof. A large crew spread throughout the hull does make it tougher to knock out than it looks. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
il_m113a1_tow: Giraf was the IDF name for TOW-armed M113A1s, one of many roles filled by Israel's 6,000-plus M113s, until Spike-armed versions took over. In the game it carries ten BGM-71C I-TOW missiles, flying at nearly 300 m/s to almost 4 km, plus a 12.7 mm machine gun, and 20 degrees of depression suit hull-down positions. The chassis struggles on slopes, and the thin armour can be pierced by autocannons or, on the flanks, heavy machine guns, so patient play from behind ridges or teammates is essential. It is a niche vehicle on most maps, but in the right spot it can hold an area. It arrived in the "Air Superiority" update.
il_m163_vulcan: Hovet, meaning "batsman", was Israel's name for the American M163 Vulcan, which joined the air defence command in 1975, scored its first kill in the 1982 Lebanon War and served for more than twenty years. In the game it is identical to the American version: its six-barrelled M168 cannon fires 3,000 rounds per minute, but there is no search radar and its effective range is short. The aluminium M113 chassis gives little protection, though it is nimble and quick. It arrived with the first Israeli tree in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_m48a1_patton_III: Magach, Hebrew for "battering ram", was Israel's name for its M48 Pattons, of which about 120 were in service when the Six-Day War began; more were captured from Jordan during that war, and most were later rebuilt to Magach 3 standard. In the game this M48A1 offers good mobility, solid armour and a capable 90 mm gun with HEATFS and APCBC rounds, and it works well following just behind more heavily armoured tanks and picking its shots. It has no gun stabiliser, which makes firing on the move difficult, and its tall silhouette is hard to hide. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
